info.name: Onboarding — Happy Path
info.description:
Driver onboarding via the BOT flow, MSIL_PARTNER / Delhi. Ported from the `MSIL Integration tests` Postman collection; each Postman folder becomes one `_group` section (the dashboard parser is flat-only, so sections are consecutive items sharing a `_group` label).

SECTIONS (in run order)
  1. Admin Login        — dashboard admin sanity + merchant/city scoping + operator role ACL
  2. Operator Onboarding — create the MSIL operator, log it in, read back its referral code
  3. DCO Onboarding      — driver signup -> docs -> hub request -> operator link -> two BOT
                           review rounds (Medical/DrivingSchool uploaded between) -> profile
                           asserting verified + enabled + approved. Ports the Postman
                           'DCO Onboarding' folder.
  4. DCO Vehicle         — adds a vehicle under that same driver: RC + 12 vehicle documents ->
                           operator hub inspection -> BOT review, ending with the VRC asserted
                           verified + approved. Ports the Postman 'DCO/Vehicle' folder.
  5. Fleet Onboarding    — individual fleet owner: login -> Aadhaar/PAN/address documents ->
                           fleet registration -> register/status -> BOT review + approval,
                           ending with the fleet asserted verified + enabled. Ports the
                           'Fleet Driver, Vehicle onboarding' collection's folder 1.
  6. Fleet Vehicle       — adds a vehicle under that fleet owner: RC + addVehicle + 13 vehicle
                           documents -> operator hub inspection -> BOT review, ending with the
                           VRC asserted verified + approved. Ports that collection's folder 3.

  7. Fleet Driver        — fleet owner adds a driver (joining OTP + documents via dashboard),
                           the driver then logs into the driver app and uploads only the
                           profile photo, followed by operator inspection and two BOT rounds,
                           ending with the driver asserted verified + enabled + approved.
                           Ports that collection's folder 4.

TOKENS
  - `POST /user/login` (step 01) yields NO usable token locally: the deployment sets
    is2faMandatory=true while the seeded admin has is2faEnabled=false, so the response
    carries authToken="". Step 01 is therefore a credential/identity check only.
  - `dashboard_token_ny` (env) is the bootstrap credential only: the NAMMA_YATRI/Bangalore
    admin registration_token seeded by provider-dashboard.sql. It is used once, by
    Admin Login step 02.
  - `msilAdminToken` (collection variable) is minted by step 02's switchMerchantAndCity
    response and is THE admin credential for every MSIL_PARTNER/Delhi dashboard call
    from step 03 onwards, including later flows.
  - `bot_dashboard_token` (env) is the seeded BOT-role token used by the BOT review steps.
  - `dashboard_token` (env) is the seeded MSIL_PARTNER/Delhi admin token. Unused while the
    Admin Login section runs first; kept as the fallback for running a later flow standalone.

WHAT IS HARDCODED vs GENERATED
  - Seeded dashboard tokens live in the env file: they are created by
    dev/local-testing-data/provider-dashboard.sql and bot-flow-config.sql, so they are
    stable per stack and must NOT be regenerated.
  - Document payloads (DL/RC/PAN/Aadhaar numbers, names, DOBs) are hardcoded because the
    mock services key their canned responses off those exact values.
  - Per-entity identifiers that must not collide across concurrent runs (driver mobile
    number, etc.) are generated in the collection-level prerequest script — see Rules.md.

PREREQUISITE: transporter_config for the Delhi opCity must have enable_bot_flow=true (+ requires_onboarding_inspection / enable_pull_pending_doc_verification). Seed via Backend/dev/local-testing-data/bot-flow-config.sql, applied by config-sync (which restarts driver-app to clear the in-process config cache).

Needs the stack: `, run-mobility-stack-dev` + `, run-test-context-server`.

exec: // Credential check only — this step deliberately captures NO token.
// Local deployments run with is2faMandatory=true and is2faEnabled=false, so
// password login resolves the person but returns authToken="" with the message
// '2 Factor authentication is not enabled, it is mandatory for this deployment'.
// The MSIL admin credential is minted in step 02 instead, from the seeded
// registration_token — see the TOKENS note in the collection description.
console.log('is2faMandatory:', d.is2faMandatory, '| is2faEnabled:', d.is2faEnabled, '| merchantId:', d.merchantId, '| city:', d.city, '| message:', d.message);
// Exercises cross-merchant access: the Bangalore/NAMMA_YATRI-scoped admin token is
// re-scoped to MSIL_PARTNER/Delhi and a fresh LoginRes.authToken comes back.
// That token is stored as `msilAdminToken` and is THE admin credential for every
// later MSIL_PARTNER/Delhi dashboard call in this and subsequent flows.
// Requests take the City by name ('Delhi'); responses serialise it as an STD code
// ('std:011'), hence the separate dashboard_city_std env var.
// Proves the token minted by step 02 really is scoped to MSIL_PARTNER/Delhi,
// rather than trusting the switch response alone.

item.name: 4 - Grant Operator Role API Access — fleetOperatorInfo (Dashboard)

exec: // operator_role_id is the DASHBOARD_OPERATOR role seeded by config-sync
// access_matrix row, so re-running this step is safe.
// Fresh operator identity on EVERY execution of this step.
// operator/register rejects an already-used mobile OR email with
// 400 INVALID_REQUEST 'Phone or Email already registered'. The dashboard's variable
// store survives between runs, so a `if (!get(...))` guard would replay the previous
// run's number and fail on the second run. Unguarded = idempotent across re-runs.
// The dashboard-facing route returns APISuccess ({"result":"Success"}) — the personId
// lives only on the internal BPP helper, so operatorId is captured later from
// Unauthenticated by design — this is the operator's own login, not an admin call.
// OTP is the fixed fake-SMS value (transporter_config.useFakeSms) — env var login_otp.
// Reads back with the operator's OWN token, which proves the DASHBOARD_OPERATOR role
// really did get GET_DRIVER_FLEET_OPERATOR_INFO from Admin Login step 04.
// This is also where operatorId comes from: operator/register returns only APISuccess.
// for MSIL/Delhi; the driver's link-to-operator step later consumes it.
// Every per-run identity is minted here, unguarded, so re-runs never replay a value that
// is already registered. Each is safe to randomise for a specific reason:
//   mobile  — pure identity, nothing validates it against a mock.
//   DL      — register/dl only checks FORMAT (validateByRegex, and the MSIL/Delhi doc config
//             carries no regex rules); the extraction match is skipped entirely because the
//             body sends dateOfIssue (DriverLicense.hs:164). Gridline's webhook then echoes
//             back whatever number was submitted, so it verifies VALID.
//   aadhaar — the SDK path verifies against the hyperverge mock override we register in
//             step 16 with these same values, so mock and request agree by construction.
//   PAN     — generated in step 18, immediately before /idfy/configure pins it.
function digits(n){ var s=''; for (var i=0;i<n;i++) s += Math.floor(Math.random()*10); return s; }
// Not in the Postman folder, which relied on a dco_driver_id left in the environment
// by an earlier manual run. The hub-request and BOT steps need it, so capture it here.
console.log('at signup — verified:', d.verified, 'enabled:', d.enabled, 'approved:', d.approved);
// Captured for the BOT Rejection Flow: rejecting a document whose invalidation is
// image-only requires the real imageId, else the reject is a silent no-op.
// Keyed on the per-run transactionId so the masked number the mock returns matches
// the one the register call submits. Overrides auto-expire after 5 minutes.

item.name: 18 - Configure Mock IDFY — per-run PAN (Mock Server)

exec: // PAN is generated here rather than at signup so it is set immediately before the
// mock is told about it — register/pancard compares the submitted panNumber against
// what idfy extracts (DriverOnboardingV2.hs:840), so the two must not drift.
function digits(n){ var s=''; for (var i=0;i<n;i++) s += Math.floor(Math.random()*10); return s; }
function letters(n){ var A='ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ', s=''; for (var i=0;i<n;i++) s += A[Math.floor(Math.random()*26)]; return s; }
// The DCO driver's Aadhaar comes from the driver-app OTP mock (MSIL SAN / 1990-01-01),
// not idfy (TEST FLEET OWNER / 1990-01-01), so the PAN<->Aadhaar cross-check can never
// pass for this persona. Pin the 4th char to a non-'P' (BUSINESS) so the check is
// deterministically skipped instead of tripping on ~1 run in 26.
// NB: pm.collectionVariables and pm.environment are SEPARATE stores in this
// must be read with collectionVariables.get — environment.get returns ''.
// The mock echoes its whole _CONFIG back — assert it really took our PAN, otherwise
// step 20 fails later with the far less obvious 'PAN number not matching'.
// Replaces the hardcoded operationHubId (a444a56a-…) in the Postman folder.
pm.test('at least one hub for MSIL/Delhi', () => pm.expect(hubs).to.be.an('array').that.is.not.empty);
// operatorCode from Operator Onboarding step 08, replacing the hardcoded "000002".
// Wait for the hub request to drain from KV to Postgres before reading it back.
// /ui/operation/createRequest writes to KV; this endpoint queries Postgres via
// findAllRequestsInRange, so the row is invisible until the drainer moves it.
// Measured on this stack: 0.1s, 9.8s and 22.0s for three create->visible cycles — the
// drainer walks one stream shard per cycle across ~128 shards, so latency swings widely.
// A fixed busy-wait long enough to cover 22s trips newman's 30s script cap and would freeze
// the dashboard UI, so poll instead: it exits as soon as the row appears.
// Requires the drainer running (DRIVER_DRAINER_STOP unset in cluster redis).
if (rows.length > 0) { console.log('hub request drained after ~' + tries + 's'); return; }
if (tries >= MAX) { console.log('[WARN] not drained after ' + tries + 's — check DRIVER_DRAINER_STOP'); return; }
// Filtered SERVER-side by mbDriverId (a real query param on GetDriverOperatorFetchHubRequests,
// Operator/Endpoints/Driver.hs:293) so the response can only contain this driver's requests.
// The driverId re-check below is belt-and-braces in case the param is ever ignored.
console.log('rows:', rows.length, '| for this driver:', mine.length, '| driverId:', driverId);
pm.test('a PENDING inspection request exists for this driver', () => pm.expect(mine.length).to.be.above(0));
pm.test('no other driver in the response', () => pm.expect(mine.length).to.eql(rows.length));
console.log('hubRequestId:', mine[0].id, '| type:', mine[0].requestType, '| status:', mine[0].requestStatus);
// Approving the DRIVER_ONBOARDING_INSPECTION created earlier is what moves
// DriverInspectionHub to VALID; without it the BOT rounds below cannot enable the driver.
// The operator's hub approval is a KV write; getInspectionHubStatusAndReason reads the Postgres
// replica, so until the drainer flushes it InspectionHub still reads PENDING and the recompute
// computes verified=false — permanently, because register/status is hit only once. Gate on the
// request actually being APPROVED in Postgres (a DB-backed read), then recompute.
pm.sendRequest({ url: url, method: 'GET', header: { token: tok } }, function (err, res) {
if (rows.length > 0) { console.log('hub request APPROVED in PG after ~' + tries + 's'); return; }
if (tries >= MAX) { console.log('[FAIL] hub request never drained to APPROVED in ' + MAX + 's'); return; }
// Hitting register/status after the operator approval drives the onboarding-flag recompute
// instead of waiting for it to happen on its own. Observed on a live run: hub request
// approved at 13:25:27 but driver_information.verified only flipped at 13:26:59 — over a
// minute later — which is why the BOT queue looked empty and the run stalled here.
// Surface the per-document statuses: if a later BOT step finds an empty queue, this log
// shows which mandatory document is still not VALID.
// Filter the queue by this entity instead of paging: the server CAPS mbLimit at 20
// (getDriverReviewQueueRequest: `limit = min maxLimit ...`, maxLimit = 20), and the DRIVER queue
// is every driver with verified=true/enabled=false — which accumulates across runs, so a fresh
// entity falls off page 1. mbPersonId pins it to ours regardless of how much test data exists.
// Still polled: the underlying tables are KV-ON, so the row appears only after the drainer flushes.
pm.sendRequest({ url: url, method: 'GET', header: { token: bot } }, function (err, res) {
console.log('entity in BOT queue after ~' + tries + 's'); return; }
if (tries >= MAX) { console.log('[FAIL] ' + want + ' never entered the BOT queue in ' + MAX + 's'); return; }
// mbLimit=200: the BOT review queue accumulates entities across runs (20 DRIVER rows
// already), and there is no per-entity filter — with a small page the freshly created
// entity simply is not on page 1 and the lookup silently finds nothing.
// Round 1: this driver must be sitting in the BOT_REVIEW queue before approval.
// Response is ReviewQueueResp { reviewQueue :: [ReviewQueue] } and the id is nested at
// a top-level driverId like the operator hub-request endpoint uses.
const mine = rows.filter(r => r.entityDetails && r.entityDetails.entityId === driverId);
console.log('queue rows:', rows.length, '| this driver:', mine.length, '| driverId:', driverId);
console.log('round 1 flags — verified:', q.verified, 'enabled:', q.enabled, 'approved:', q.approved);
pm.test('driver is queued for BOT review', () => pm.expect(mine.length).to.be.above(0));
// guarded: an empty queue must fail the assertion above, not throw here.
pm.test('queued entity is a DRIVER', () => pm.expect(mine[0] && mine[0].entityDetails.entityType).to.eql('DRIVER'));
// Round 1. Empty rejectDocumentUpdateReq = approve; a non-empty list rejects.
// Dashboard upload is JSON+base64 (not multipart), so it uses the env fixture string.
// Dashboard upload is JSON+base64 (not multipart), so it uses the env fixture string.
// Filter the queue by this entity instead of paging: the server CAPS mbLimit at 20
// (getDriverReviewQueueRequest: `limit = min maxLimit ...`, maxLimit = 20), and the DRIVER queue
// is every driver with verified=true/enabled=false — which accumulates across runs, so a fresh
// entity falls off page 1. mbPersonId pins it to ours regardless of how much test data exists.
// Still polled: the underlying tables are KV-ON, so the row appears only after the drainer flushes.
pm.sendRequest({ url: url, method: 'GET', header: { token: bot } }, function (err, res) {
console.log('entity in BOT queue after ~' + tries + 's'); return; }
if (tries >= MAX) { console.log('[FAIL] ' + want + ' never entered the BOT queue in ' + MAX + 's'); return; }
// mbLimit=200: the BOT review queue accumulates entities across runs (20 DRIVER rows
// already), and there is no per-entity filter — with a small page the freshly created
// entity simply is not on page 1 and the lookup silently finds nothing.
// Round 2 is informational, NOT a gate. Verified live: after the round-1 approval the
// driver legitimately LEAVES the BOT_REVIEW queue, so requiring presence here fails on
// a correct run. The round-2 submit/review/request still returns 200 and is what lets
// the freshly uploaded Medical/DrivingSchool certificates settle the enabling docs.
const mine = rows.filter(r => r.entityDetails && r.entityDetails.entityId === driverId);
console.log('round 2 — queue rows:', rows.length, '| this driver still queued:', mine.length > 0);
// Round 2. Empty rejectDocumentUpdateReq = approve; a non-empty list rejects.

item.name: 38 - Driver Profile — assert verified + enabled + approved (Driver)

exec: // register/status is the recompute trigger and is hit exactly once, by its own step —
// re-running it inside a poll re-recomputes the flags and can undo a BOT approval.
// Poll the plain read instead; driver_information is PG-backed (KV disabled), so the
// value is visible as soon as the write lands.
pm.sendRequest({ url: purl, method: 'GET', header: { token: tok } }, function (err, res) {
var d = {}; try { d = res.json() || {}; } catch (e) {}
if (d.approved === true) { console.log('approved after ~' + tries + 's'); return; }
if (tries >= MAX) { console.log('[WARN] approved still ' + d.approved + ' after ' + tries + 's'); return; }
// Success condition for the whole DCO sequence.
// Per-run RC so the section is idempotent: a repeat registration number collides on the
// vehicle_registration_certificate uniqueness check. Prefix must be in the MSIL/Delhi
function digits(n){ var s=''; for (var i=0;i<n;i++) s += Math.floor(Math.random()*10); return s; }
function letters(n){ var A='ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ', s=''; for (var i=0;i<n;i++) s += A[Math.floor(Math.random()*26)]; return s; }
// compares vehicleAge.getMonths), and gridline's default registration_date of 2021-12-28 is
// ~56 months old — it only slips through because an absent age makes the comparison vacuous.
// Compute a date 12 months back so the rule is satisfied deliberately, and so this never
// goes stale the way a hardcoded date would.
// The age rule reads rc.mYManufacturing (VehicleRegistrationCertificate.hs:712), NOT the
// registration date, and it is fed by the Idfy field m_y_manufacturing (Interface/Idfy.hs:612)
// as YYYY-MM (the handler appends -01). Left unset it is Nothing, and Nothing <= Just 36 is
// vacuously true — so the rule would silently never be exercised.
// Keyed on the per-run RC. Two config gates decide whether the RC verifies:
//   {cab,pcv,lpv,passenger commercial vehicle,light passenger vehicle} — the Postman
//   collection sent LMV, which fails with 'Vehicles like LMV are not allowed for this
//   service' and leaves the RC INVALID. LPV is in that list AND in the DVC's supported
//   vehicle classes (variant TAXI), so it satisfies both.
//   rc_validation_rules.vehicle_oem is nulled by bot-flow-config.sql, so the manufacturer
//   below is not rejected by validateRCResponse's InvalidOEM check.
//   fuel_type must be in {Petrol,Diesel,CNG,LPG,EV,Electric}, and m_y_manufacturing must be
//   within max_vehicle_age (36 MONTHS) — both pinned here rather than left to mock defaults.
// No change to gridline.py: /mock/override deep-merges into result.extraction_output
// (gridline.py:238-247), so other collections keep the untouched defaults.
// Postman sent {{RcImageId}} here while the capture set RCImageId — always an empty id.

item.name: 42 - Wait for RC registration — capture rcId (Dashboard)

exec: // register/rc returns 200 immediately but the VRC row only exists once the gridline
// webhook lands. Uploading an RC-scoped document before that fails with RC_NOT_FOUND
// (reproduced live: the same upload 400s, then succeeds a second later).
// Wait for the RC DOCUMENT to verify too, not just the row to exist: the operator
// approval checks InspectionHub dependencies and rejects with 'dependency documents
// not valid: VehicleRegistrationCertificate' while it is still PENDING.
if (v.rcId && v.verificationStatus === 'VALID') { console.log('RC VALID after ~' + tries + 's'); return; }
if (tries >= MAX) { console.log('[WARN] RC still ' + v.verificationStatus + ' after ' + tries + 's'); return; }
// rcId is the VRC uuid — the entityId the BOT review takes for a VEHICLE.
console.log('rcId:', v.rcId, '| status:', v.verificationStatus, '| approved:', v.approved);
// Captured for the BOT Rejection Flow: rejecting a document whose invalidation is
// image-only requires the real imageId, else the reject is a silent no-op.

// image-only requires the real imageId, else the reject is a silent no-op.

// image-only requires the real imageId, else the reject is a silent no-op.

// image-only requires the real imageId, else the reject is a silent no-op.
// Captured for the BOT Rejection Flow: rejecting a document whose invalidation is
// image-only requires the real imageId, else the reject is a silent no-op.
// Same KV->Postgres drain race as the driver hub request: createRequest writes to KV,
// this endpoint reads Postgres. Measured 0.1-22s on this stack, so poll rather than wait.
if (rows.length > 0) { console.log('vehicle hub request drained after ~' + tries + 's'); return; }
if (tries >= MAX) { console.log('[WARN] not drained after ' + tries + 's'); return; }
// Scoped to THIS run's registration number so a leftover request is never approved.
console.log('rows:', rows.length, '| for this RC:', mine.length, '| rc:', rc);
pm.test('a PENDING inspection request exists for this vehicle', () => pm.expect(mine.length).to.be.above(0));

item.name: 59 - Recompute vehicle after hub approval drained (Dashboard)

exec: // The operator's hub approval is a KV write; getInspectionHubStatusAndReason reads the Postgres
// replica, so until the drainer flushes it InspectionHub still reads PENDING and the recompute
// computes verified=false — permanently, because register/status is hit only once. Gate on the
// request actually being APPROVED in Postgres (a DB-backed read), then recompute.
pm.sendRequest({ url: url, method: 'GET', header: { token: tok } }, function (err, res) {
if (rows.length > 0) { console.log('hub request APPROVED in PG after ~' + tries + 's'); return; }
if (tries >= MAX) { console.log('[FAIL] hub request never drained to APPROVED in ' + MAX + 's'); return; }
// Single hit — vehicleStatus IS the vehicle recompute trigger. It runs only after the
// gate above confirms the hub approval is visible in Postgres.
console.log('59 - BOT Review Queue — VEHI after hub approval — verified:', v.verified, 'approved:', v.approved);
// Filter the queue by this entity instead of paging: the server CAPS mbLimit at 20
// (getDriverReviewQueueRequest: `limit = min maxLimit ...`, maxLimit = 20), and the DRIVER queue
// is every driver with verified=true/enabled=false — which accumulates across runs, so a fresh
// entity falls off page 1. mbRcId pins it to ours regardless of how much test data exists.
// Still polled: the underlying tables are KV-ON, so the row appears only after the drainer flushes.
pm.sendRequest({ url: url, method: 'GET', header: { token: bot } }, function (err, res) {
console.log('entity in BOT queue after ~' + tries + 's'); return; }
if (tries >= MAX) { console.log('[FAIL] ' + want + ' never entered the BOT queue in ' + MAX + 's'); return; }
// mbLimit=200: the BOT review queue accumulates entities across runs (20 DRIVER rows
// already), and there is no per-entity filter — with a small page the freshly created
// entity simply is not on page 1 and the lookup silently finds nothing.
const mine = rows.filter(r => r.entityDetails && (r.entityDetails.entityId === rcId || r.entityDetails.rcNo === rc));
console.log('VEHICLE queue rows:', rows.length, '| this vehicle queued:', mine.length > 0);
// The BOT approve is synchronous — verified live: approved flips False->True in the same
// call (unified_onboarding_flags_recompute is NULL for MSIL/Delhi, so the handler takes the
// direct QVRC.updateApproved branch). But hitting register/status afterwards runs
// which recomputes approved from documents WITHOUT forcing BotApproval valid and resets it
// to false. An earlier version of this step polled register/status and undid its own
if (v.approved === true && v.verificationStatus === 'VALID') { console.log('vehicle settled after ~' + tries + 's'); return; }
if (tries >= MAX) { console.log('[WARN] vehicle status=' + v.verificationStatus + ' approved=' + v.approved); return; }
// Success condition for the vehicle section.

item.name: 63 - Configure Mock IDFY — per-run fleet Aadhaar/PAN (Mock Server)

exec: // Per-run fleet identity, unguarded so re-runs never replay a registered mobile/PAN/Aadhaar.
// The onboarding/verify/VERIFY_PAN and VERIFY_AADHAAR calls compare the submitted number
// against what idfy extracts, so the mock must be told these values FIRST — same contract
// as the driver PAN step earlier in this collection.
function digits(n){ var s=''; for (var i=0;i<n;i++) s += Math.floor(Math.random()*10); return s; }
function letters(n){ var A='ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ', s=''; for (var i=0;i<n;i++) s += A[Math.floor(Math.random()*26)]; return s; }
// 4th char 'P' => INDIVIDUAL PAN. We only cover individual fleets right now, and a
// business PAN would set skipPanAadhaarCrossCheck, silently skipping the PAN<->Aadhaar
// cross-check this flow is meant to exercise.
// The V2 login/verify pair does not return the personId, so read it from the dashboard
// profile with the fleet's own token. MSILOnboarding resolves this with a raw SQL select
// against the person table; /user/profile is the same answer without the DB dependency.
// The source folder repeats the JSON key "imageId" twice for front and back, so the back
// silently overwrites the front. optionalImageId is the real field for the second image.
// Captured for the BOT Rejection Flow: rejecting a document whose invalidation is
// image-only requires the real imageId, else the reject is a silent no-op.
// PAN verification is asynchronous. Registering before it lands leaves the fleet short of
// a mandatory document, so it never reaches the BOT queue. Poll the fleet's own info until
// the docs settle rather than racing it.
// operatorReferralCode reuses the operator created in the Operator Onboarding section,
// replacing the hardcoded referral code in the source collection.
// Same role as in the DCO section: hitting register/status drives the onboarding-flag
// recompute so the fleet shows up in the BOT review queue.

item.name: 75 - Fleet Owner Info — before BOT approval (Dashboard)

console.log('entity in BOT queue after ~' + tries + 's'); return; }

item.name: 78 - Fleet Owner Info — assert verified + enabled + approved (Dashboard)

exec: // Deliberately does NOT call register/status here — in the vehicle section that recompute
// undid a fresh BOT approval. Poll the fleet info only.
if (d.enabled === true) { console.log('fleet enabled after ~' + tries + 's'); return; }
if (tries >= MAX) { console.log('[WARN] fleet enabled=' + d.enabled + ' approved=' + d.approved); return; }
// Success condition for the fleet section.
